validated_work_order.understanding: The weekly end-bound suite exists twice: in packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts (338 lines, 10 `it`) and inside the larger custom-spreadsheet.test.ts (1100 lines, carrying all 10 of those titles under `weekly custom report end bound` (7) and `weekly grouped report end bound` (3)). I diffed the two describe blocks rather than taking the epic's word for it: `diff <(sed -n '181,338p' weekly-end-date.test.ts) <(sed -n '380,549p' custom-spreadsheet.test.ts)` returns exactly ten hunks, and every one is the props wrapper alone — `runCustom({ endDate: '2026-10-03' })` vs `runCustom(weeklyProps({ endDate: '2026-10-03' }))`, and the same for the three grouped cases. Not one assertion, expected value, comment or fixture differs. The ten `it(...)` titles are byte-identical between the files. The `weeklyRows` fixture is byte-identical (md5 6342ab83b4f60f70b3f77d129ec0d601 in both). `weeklyProps` supplies startDate '2026-08-30', interval 'Weekly', firstDayOfWeekIdx '0', the show*/trimIntervals/groupBy/conditions defaults — precisely the defaults weekly-end-date.test.ts's own `runCustom` already defaults to — plus `balanceTypeOp: undefined`, which the shorter file omits and createCustomSpreadsheet treats identically. Its server double is the strictly weaker one: it neither splits the amount filter nor applies `$transform` precision, where the survivor's does. Every helper in the shorter file has a counterpart in the survivor, whose afterEach additionally resets `servedRows.current`. Nothing is referenced by path anywhere else in the repo. So the comparison the epic asked for comes out one way: weekly-end-date.test.ts contributes no unique case and is deleted outright. The surviving file is custom-spreadsheet.test.ts, which is also where the budgeted, category-axis, 'any of' and text-operator suites already live and which share the same server double and fixtures.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The suite was copied rather than moved into custom-spreadsheet.test.ts during a merge-conflict resolution (the epic cites merge commit 9c44b8d, not reachable in this checkout, against b593293 which is — "[AI] Fix weekly reports truncating the final week to one day (#12)"). b593293 added the ten cases to custom-spreadsheet.test.ts; a later merge left a second copy in a file of its own, and nothing since has removed it. The last commit touching either file, 026f8b6, is the #9 category-filtering fix — the copy is actively maintained in both.
validated_work_order.approach: Delete weekly-end-date.test.ts outright and change nothing else. No case needs to move: the ten titles and their bodies already exist in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts, verified by diff rather than by eye, so the epic's "fold back whatever it uniquely adds" reduces to a plain delete. custom-spreadsheet.test.ts is not edited except for one comment recording the comparison, because editing it further would widen a diff whose whole point is that it is a deletion. The decision is recorded in the PR in the two places this repo permits — a Maintenance release note in upcoming-release-notes/, matching the precedent of merge-duplicate-themes-directories.md for an identical kind of dedup, and a short comment above the surviving describe. Note for the implementer: .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md forbids filling in the PR template, so the comparison goes in those two files, not in the PR Description section.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every claim was checked against the files rather than inferred from the issue. The ten titles diff clean, the describe-block diff shows only props-wrapper hunks, the shared fixture is md5-identical, a repo-wide grep finds no path reference to the deleted file, and the delete-or-fold decision the epic called a judgement call resolves cleanly on the evidence to 'delete outright'. The residual 5 is only that CI runs the full suite and this planner could not execute vitest in this checkout (no node_modules state file present), so the AC-5 count-delta is stated as something the implementer and QA measure rather than something I measured.

risks: The one real risk is a silent coverage loss if the diff were read only at the title level. It was not: `diff` over the two describe blocks returns hunks only in the props wrapper, and the weeklyRows fixture is byte-identical (md5 6342ab83b4f60f70b3f77d129ec0d601 in both files). A reviewer who wants to re-check that has the exact command in AC-4.

The survivor's server double is stricter than the deleted file's — it applies the `$transform` precision and splits the amount filter, which the shorter file did not. This changes nothing for these ten cases (all weeklyRows amounts are positive and the interval is Weekly), and the survivor is where these tests already run and pass today, but it is the reason the copy is the one to delete rather than the other way round.
No new hosts are contacted by this change and no data is sent anywhere, so env.api_allowlist in .sdlc/config.yml needs no addition. Nothing in forbidden_paths is touched.

The implementer must not be tempted to also delete or merge the other suites in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts (budgeted, category axis, 'any of', text operators). They are not duplicates and are out of scope.
out_of_scope: The other describes in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts (weekly budgeted, category axis narrowing, 'any of', text operators) — none is a duplicate, and none is touched.

The shared server double, fixtures and helpers inside custom-spreadsheet.test.ts. Deleting the other file leaves them with a single caller; simplifying them is a separate change and would enlarge this diff.
Any duplication between these two files' shapes and other test files elsewhere in the suite. The epic raised this one pair; the next pair, if it exists, is its own ticket.
Running the desktop-client suite faster. Dropping ten duplicate tests is the ticket; profiling or re-sharding the suite is not.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete weekly-end-date.test.ts and move anything unique into custom-spreadsheet.test.ts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is nothing to move. The diff over the two describe blocks is empty of content — the ten titles are byte-identical and the bodies differ only in the props wrapper, whose defaults are the ones the shorter file already defaulted to. This was the epic's first option and it reduces to a plain delete.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep weekly-end-date.test.ts and delete the ten cases from custom-spreadsheet.test.ts instead.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It keeps the weaker of the two suites. The surviving copy would lose the server double that applies `$transform` precision and splits the amount filter, and it would strand the `weeklyProps` helper, which the weekly budgeted describe also uses. It also means editing a 1100-line file to delete ten cases, rather than deleting a 338-line file outright.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extract the ten cases plus their fixtures and server double into a shared test helper both files import.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves both files running the same ten cases, which is the duplication the ticket exists to remove — it hides the duplication behind an import instead of ending it, and it adds a new shared helper to a codebase that is trying to lose a file, not gain a layer.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep both files but mark the ten cases in weekly-end-date.test.ts `it.skip`, or move them under a single shared describe imported by both.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Skipped tests still count in a reportable total and rot silently; the shared-describe form keeps two files alive for one suite. Either leaves the 338 lines a reviewer is asked to judge, which the ticket names as half the cost.

assumptions: main is the base branch — .sdlc/config.yml leaves base_branch empty, which means the repo default, and the issue's own verification is against main.

Vitest discovers test files by glob rather than by an explicit list. No vitest config names either file, and a repo-wide grep finds no path reference to weekly-end-date.test.ts, so nothing has to be unlisted along with the deletion.
unknowns: The epic cites merge commit 9c44b8d as the conflict resolution that moved the suite out. That object is not reachable in this checkout, so the copy's exact provenance is taken from the issue. It does not affect the decision — the duplication is present on main either way, which is what the diff shows.
residual_risks: The AC-1 and AC-5 test-count deltas are the only claims here that were not directly executed, because this checkout has no node_modules state and vitest cannot start. Both are stated as measurements to take against main, not as results.
